national_raw_news.title: Vice President hoists National Flag in Andaman and Nicobar Islands as part of ‘Har Ghar Tiranga Campaign’
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 2:19 PM Vice President hoists National Flag in Andaman and Nicobar Islands as part of ‘Har Ghar Tiranga Campaign’ Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan today hoisted the National Flag at the Flag Point in Sri Vijaya Puram, the capital of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, as part of the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga Campaign’. On the occasion, he paid tribute to the brave freedom fighters. The Vice President also attended the state function, ‘Tiranga Concert on Vande Mataram’, held at the auditorium of Dr B. R. Ambedkar Institute of Technology. In his address, the Vice President recalled the glorious history of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands associated with India’s freedom struggle. He said this is the very land where freedom fighters endured severe torture and unimaginable hardships for the country’s independence. Referring to the historical significance of the Cellular Jail, Mr Radhakrishnan paid homage to the sacrifices and contributions of the freedom fighters. He also recalled the historic day of 30th December 1943, when Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose hoisted the Tricolour in Port Blair. The Vice President said that whenever the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are mentioned, one not only thinks of their natural beauty and lush greenery but also remembers the spirit of patriotism associated with Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose hoisting the Tricolour here for the first time. Referring to the significance of ‘Vande Mataram’, the Vice President said that the song played an important role in strengthening the spirit of nationalism and unity among the people during the freedom movement. He described the Andaman and Nicobar Islands as a symbol of India’s diversity and unity. He also emphasised the need to maintain a balance between the country’s development and environmental protection. Mr Radhakrishnan is on a two-day visit to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Yesterday, he visited the National Memorial Cellular Jail and paid tribute to the brave freedom fighters. He also visited Veer Savarkar’s cell and witnessed the light and sound show organised at the Cellular Jail.

national_raw_news.title: Har Ghar Tiranga campaign begins with multiple events across country to celebrate patriotism and national unity
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 2:03 PM Har Ghar Tiranga campaign begins with multiple events across country to celebrate patriotism and national unity The Har Ghar Tiranga campaign is being celebrated nationwide to foster a sense of patriotism among citizens, strengthen national unity, and promote India’s cultural heritage. The campaign marks the fifth year of the Har Ghar Tiranga initiative, which began in 2022 and has since evolved into one of the country’s largest public participation movements. The initiative is aimed at encouraging citizens to hoist the National Flag and participate in activities celebrating patriotism, national unity and India’s cultural heritage. This year’s campaign holds special significance as it coincides with the 150th anniversary of India’s National Song, “Vande Mataram,” bringing together the National Flag and the National Song in a unique celebration of patriotism. As part of the celebrations, mass singing of Vande Mataram will be organised across the country. In Delhi, as part of the campaign, Lok Sabha BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj paid floral tribute at the memorial of Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya in Malviya Nagar followed by a Tiranga Yatra from Pilanji Village to Greater Kailash. Speaking to the media, Ms Swaraj said that this Independence Day is particularly special as India marks its 80th. She added that the BJP has launched a week-long campaign starting today, during which party office-bearers and workers will visit the memorials of national heroes and martyrs.

national_raw_news.title: NIA arrests one more accused in connection with seizure of huge consignment of illegal explosives in Malappuram, Keralam
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 1:50 PM NIA arrests one more accused in connection with seizure of huge consignment of illegal explosives in Malappuram, Keralam The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has arrested another accused in connection with the seizure of a huge consignment of illegal explosives in Malappuram, Keralam. The Agency informed that the accused was arrested yesterday from Manjeri in the Malappuram district. NIA said that the accused is a main conspirator and was involved in the illegal procurement of the explosives seized in the case. The latest arrest comes a day after the NIA arrested three more accused from Vijayapura in Karnataka on Friday, taking the total number of arrests in the case to ten. The case relates to the seizure of 89,600 explosive sticks and 10,500 shock tubes from a lorry parked in the compound of Farha Hollow Bricks Company on the Chemmad-Thalappara Road in Malappuram. NIA further said that investigation into the larger conspiracy and the illegal procurement and movement of the explosives is continuing.

national_raw_news.title: NBA disburses over 3 crore rupees under Access and Benefit Sharing mechanism to 33 States/UTs and National Institutes
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 1:21 PM NBA disburses over 3 crore rupees under Access and Benefit Sharing mechanism to 33 States/UTs and National Institutes The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed over 3 crore rupees as Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) to 33 State Biodiversity Boards, Union Territory Biodiversity Councils and National Institutes. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change said that the release covers a diverse range of India’s agrobiodiversity, including tomato, chilli, brinjal and deep-frozen Sahiwal cattle semen. It informed that cumulative ABS disbursements by the NBA have now exceeded 166 crore rupees. The Ministry also said that each release further strengthens the link between biodiversity conservation, scientific research and the livelihoods of the communities that conserve India’s rich biological resources. national_raw_news.title: Appointment of 30 Judges for High Courts of Madras, Calcutta, Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka notified
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 8:29 AM Appointment of 30 Judges for High Courts of Madras, Calcutta, Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka notified The Centre has notified the appointment of 30 judges for High Courts of Madras, Calcutta, Madhya Pradesh, and Karnataka, with Madras High Court receiving the largest share of new appointees. According to a notification issued by the Ministry of Law and Justice, the appointments include 20 advocates and 10 judicial officers. Of the total, 15 judges have been appointed to the Madras High Court, 8 to the Calcutta High Court, 6 to the Karnataka High Court and one to the Madhya Pradesh High Court. The appointments were made by the President in consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Supreme Court Collegium. The newly appointed judges are expected to take an oath and assume office in the coming days. The appointments are expected to help fill vacancies in the four High Courts and improve the disposal of pending cases. national_raw_news.title: Amarnath Yatra to remain suspended from both Pahalgam and Baltal routes
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 8:20 AM Amarnath Yatra to remain suspended from both Pahalgam and Baltal routes In Jammu and Kashmir, the annual Amarnath Yatra will remain suspended on both the Pahalgam and Baltal routes from today due to recent rains, repair work of pilgrimage tracks and the forecast of adverse weather conditions over the next few days. The decision to temporarily halt the yatra has been taken keeping in view the condition of the tracks as well as the weather forecast issued by the India Meteorological Department. No fresh Yatra convoy was allowed to leave the Bhagwati Nagar base camp in Jammu yesterday as a precautionary measure amid rains and inclement weather conditions prevailing in Ramban district and parts of Kashmir. Meanwhile, the 28th batch, comprising 1,202 pilgrims who had completed darshan at the Holy Cave and were staying at the Baltal base camp, was allowed to proceed towards Jammu in a convoy of 44 vehicles. The returning pilgrims included 867 males, 251 females, one child, 79 sadhus and four sadhvis. The convoy comprised 28 heavy vehicles, one medium motor vehicle, 11 light motor vehicles and four trucks. 3336 pilgrims performed darshan at the Holy Cave yesterday. The pilgrims included 2384 males, 569 females, 21 children, 20 sadhus, six sadhvis, four transgender pilgrims and 332 security personnel. With this, the total number of pilgrims who have performed darshan during the 2026 Yatra has reached 4 lakh 80 thousand and 19. The 57-day-long Amarnath Yatra commenced on July 3 simultaneously from both the traditional Chandanwari route in Anantnag district and the Baltal route in Ganderbal district and is scheduled to culminate with the traditional Chadi Mubarak ceremony on August 28. However, due to the recent rains, a necessity for the repair and maintenance of the Yatra tracks at vulnerable stretches has been felt, which is being undertaken by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO). The IMD has predicted adverse weather conditions over the next few days. Hence, the Yatra shall remain suspended from both routes with effect from today. Authorities have appealed to pilgrims to follow advisories issued by the competent authorities from time to time in the interest of their safety and the smooth conduct of the pilgrimage.

national_raw_news.title: Pentagon orders US defense companies to accelerate weapons production and deliveries
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 10:19 AM Pentagon orders US defense companies to accelerate weapons production and deliveries WASHINGTON, Aug. 2, 2019 (Xinhua) -- The Pentagon is seen from an airplane over Washington D.C., the United States, on July 11, 2018. The United States will fully develop ground-launched conventional missiles after withdrawing from the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces (INF) Treaty, U.S. Secretary of Defense Mark Esper said Friday. (Xinhua/Liu Jie/IANS) The Pentagon has ordered US defense companies to accelerate weapons production and deliveries as the Iran war has depleted key US munitions stockpiles. The Washington Post reported that Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg told defense industry leaders in a memo that they have 21 days to submit plans to drive significantly faster, more aggressive delivery schedules and increased production for critical capabilities. The Pentagon has also pursued framework agreements with major defense contractors and technology firms to expand production. But those agreements are nonbinding and depend on congressional funding. The directive comes as the Pentagon seeks to replenish stocks of weapons, including Patriot and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) interceptors. The Center for Strategic and International Studies said the global inventory of Patriot missiles had fallen from about 2,200 before the war to fewer than 827, while THAAD stocks dropped from 452 to less than 278. The Pentagon’s push comes as a 1.15 trillion US Dollar defense spending bill remains stalled in Congress, potentially delaying efforts to rapidly expand weapons production.

national_raw_news.title: Health Minister Nadda Releases Knowledge Paper on AI in Medical Technology
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 8, 2026 10:22 PM Health Minister Nadda Releases Knowledge Paper on AI in Medical Technology Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda today released the knowledge paper, ‘AI in MedTech: Revolutionizing Healthcare Through Artificial Intelligence’, at India Medical Device 2026 in New Delhi. The Health Ministry said the report outlines five key priorities for accelerating the responsible adoption of AI in healthcare. These range from AI-ready data and evidence, lifecycle-based regulation and reimbursement mechanisms, to scaling up AI-enabled diagnostics and strengthening collaboration across government, industry, healthcare and academia. The report highlights India’s opportunity to leverage its digital public infrastructure, software capabilities, clinical diversity and growing MedTech manufacturing base to emerge as a global leader in responsible AI-enabled medical technologies.
